method.title: How Grid Watch works
method.intro: Grid Watch estimates electricity supply stress in Curaçao during the evening peak, from public weather data and published figures only. It is an experimental research project by Noir Visuals, not an operational utility forecast, and it is not affiliated with Aqualectra, MDC or RAC.
method.number.p: Each evening gets a stress index from 0 to 100, calculated with fixed, published rules ({name} version {version}). It is not a probability: the rules have not been calibrated against real events yet. The level follows from the index: Low below {moderate}, Moderate from {moderate}, Elevated from {elevated} and High from {high}.
method.inputs.p: Hourly forecasts of wind at about 100 m (turbine hub height), temperature and humidity for the evening window {start} to {end} Curaçao time, for the next {days} days. Wind is read at the wind parks, heat at the Dokweg area where demand is concentrated. Source: {provider}, model {model}; the ensemble ({ensemble}) gives the spread for the confidence label.
method.rules.wind: Estimated wind output: a generic turbine power curve, zero below {cutIn} m/s and from {cutOut} m/s, full output from {rated} m/s, growing with the cube of the wind speed in between. It is the island total, not measured production.
method.rules.windStress: Wind stress: none while the estimated output is {noStress} % or more, rising to full when the turbines stand still.
method.rules.demand: Demand proxy: the evening heat index, scaled from 0 at {low} °C to 1 at {high} °C. Normal below {raised}, raised from {raised}, high from {highFrom}.
method.rules.index: Stress index = 100 × ({wWind} × wind stress + {wDemand} × demand proxy). Wind weighs more because it is the biggest swing factor on the island.
method.rules.sites: Wind park status: High below {highBelow} m/s, Elevated below {elevatedBelow} m/s, otherwise Low. The three wind locations share the island-wide figure; output is not split by park. Dokweg is always "not public".
method.rules.confidence: Confidence: high for the first two days, medium up to day {medium}, low after that, and one step lower when the ensemble members disagree by more than {spread} m/s.
method.gaps.p: Which generators are running or in maintenance, the real electricity demand, battery charge, and measured output per wind park. Only the utility has those numbers. Recent outages were partly caused by units in maintenance, which no weather-based rule can see.
method.record.p: The outlook is calculated twice a day. Every issuance is stored unchanged with its inputs, the weather model run it used and the rules version, so it can be checked later. If no new outlook arrives for {hours} hours the site shows "Data out of date" and greys out the statuses.
method.limits.p: The rules are starting assumptions, not fitted to events. The window covers the evening peak only: the island-wide blackout of 27 August 2025 started around 02:30, outside it. The next phase tests the rules against sourced events and publishes how often they were right.
method.sources.p: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0). Map data from OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Fleet figures from the RAC energy report 2024. Every source, its licence and retrieval date are listed in the project's data register.
method.news.p: News items on the site are written by the project. They never change the outlook, and reports about outages or the utility always name their source.
method.contact.p: Spotted a mistake, or represent the utility or MDC and want something corrected or removed? Open an issue on GitHub (a public source is needed for data corrections). Valid corrections are made promptly.
